title: Localized ring-sheaf mates evaluated along graphs
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme, let $u:V\to B$ be an object of its small pro-étale site with the universe convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use the inverse image $u^{-1}$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] on abelian sheaves (and its induced ring-object functor). Let $R$ and $S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $B_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$, respectively, and let $\beta:u^{-1}R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ be a ring-sheaf isomorphism. Under the restriction identification of clause (1) of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], write $\bar\beta:R|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}S$; restriction and its ring operations are those of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $e_u:R\to u_*u^{-1}R$ be the unit of the sheafified-left-Kan-extension adjunction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and put $\eta^\beta=u_*\beta\circ e_u$.

For every $T\to B$ in $B_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $a\in R(T)$, with $T\times_BV$ viewed over $V$ by the second projection, one has
$$e_{u,T}(a)=R(\operatorname{pr}_T)(a),\qquad \eta^\beta_T(a)=\bar\beta_{T\times_BV}\bigl(R(\operatorname{pr}_T)(a)\bigr),$$
where the first equality uses the stated restriction identification. For every $U\to V$ in $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and every $B$-map $b:U\to T$, let $\gamma_b=(b,U\to V):U\to T\times_BV$. Then
$$S(\gamma_b)\eta^\beta_T(a)=\bar\beta_U(R(b)(a)).$$
In particular, with $\delta:V\to V\times_BV$ the diagonal, the map $S(\delta)\eta^\beta_V$ is the ring isomorphism $\bar\beta_{V/V}:R(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(V,S)$. For a global section $r\in\Gamma(B,R)$, pullback of the map $\underline{\mathbf Z}\to R$ sending $1$ to $r$, followed by $\beta$, is the global section $\bar\beta_{V/V}(R(u)(r))$; the monoidal-unit comparison is the canonical one for inverse image.

proof.text: Expand the specified sheafified-left-Kan adjunction using restrictFullyFaithful and composition of adjunctions. Its underlying presheaf unit is the left Kan unit followed by the whiskered sheafification unit. This computes the existing proEtaleSheafAdjunction, without replacing it by an isomorphic adjunction.

proof.text: Write F for composition with V → B and G for base change, with adjunction a : F ⊣ G. Cancel the component of the inverse normalized sheaf comparison. Its sheafIso_inv and coprojection fields express it as the Kan unit at F(G(T)), restriction along the site-adjunction unit at G(T), and sheafification. Naturality of the Kan unit along the site counit F(G(T)) → T, followed by the right triangle identity of a, identifies this composite with the specified sheaf unit. Thus the normalized sheaf unit is restriction along the site counit (the first projection).

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products), product adjunction; the distinguished coprojections in clause (1) of lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction.

proof.text: Compose the normalized-unit equation with the inverse comparison and β to obtain the mate formula. Apply naturality of the localized isomorphism along the graph. The inverse Hom-equivalence identity for F ⊣ G gives F(γ_b) followed by the counit equals b. Contravariant functoriality of R then gives the graph formula as an equality of ring homomorphisms, hence on every section.

source.place: Tag 00Y0 (definition-localize), restriction formula following the definition; naturality applied to the graph.

proof.text: Specialize the graph formula to T = V, U = V/V and the identity-object isomorphism b. Both R(b) and the component of the localized ring-sheaf isomorphism are invertible, so their composite is invertible. This proves the diagonal identity and isomorphism assertion without requiring the diagonal restriction alone to be invertible.

source.place: Tag 00Y0 (definition-localize), category over V and sectionwise restriction.

proof.text: For the constant-sheaf/restriction/sheafification comparison E, its compatibility with toSheafify identifies E on constant sections. In the inverse-image adjunction, apply injectivity of homEquiv and sheafification uniqueness to prove c.hom followed by E.inv is the specified constant inverse-image map: the normalized-unit formula and naturality of toSheafify identify both adjoints on every constant section. Consequently E.hom followed by c.inv is inverse to that specified map. For a section r, naturality of the additive restriction comparison cancels the inverse-image comparisons in the definition of the pulled section. What remains is E.hom, ordinary restriction of the integer-to-R map, and the additive map of the localized ring isomorphism. The composite constant-presheaf/sheafification adjunction evaluates the integer-to-R map at an arbitrary object as n ↦ R(U → B)(n • r). The compatibility of E with toSheafify and evaluation at 1 therefore give the final formula.
